page: Amazon Web Services c6g.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the 64-bit ARMv8 AWS Graviton processor family (Neoverse-N1). The instance provides 64 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, clocked at 2.5 GHz. Each core has a private 64 KB L1 data cache and 1.0 MB L2 cache, backed by 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 128.0 GB, yielding a 1:2 ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The server does not include local storage or hardware accelerators, but it delivers a baseline network throughput of 25 Gbps.

Benchmark results highlight the advantages of a full 64-core physical topology alongside typical per-core constraints. Multi-threaded throughput ranks in the top tier, shown by a stress-ng multi-core metric of 97,056.55, a Clang compilation score of 42,910.0, and static web serving throughput reaching 45.55 GB/sec. Redis operations demonstrate high concurrent capability, achieving 77.68 million SET operations per second. In-cache memory access scales sharply, registering 3,782.53 GB/sec in 16 KB read tests, before settling into average performance tiers for large, uncached blocks (166.55 GB/sec read and 74.45 GB/sec write).

Conversely, single-threaded processing reflects the modest 2.5 GHz clock and ARM instruction design. Geekbench single-core performance ranks in the lower tier at 970.0, accompanied by lower-tier throughput in single-threaded gzip compression (20.33 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (7.58 GB/sec). Large language model generation speeds also scale down significantly as parameter counts grow, dropping to 2.74 tokens per second on 70B models due to the absence of dedicated matrix accelerators like AVX-512 or AMX.

From an efficiency perspective, the dedicated-core design avoids hyperthreading contention, delivering consistent parallel computing capability per unit of compute resources. Amazon Web Services c6g.16xlarge is best suited for horizontally parallel workloads, such as distributed CI/CD compilation pipelines, high-concurrency static web serving, containerized microservices, and in-memory key-value caching.
description: Amazon Web Services c6g.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by a 64-core AWS Graviton processor based on the ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 architecture running at 2.5 GHz. With one thread per physical core, the instance provides 64 dedicated vCPUs paired with 128.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per core) and 25 Gbps baseline networking, without local storage or GPU hardware. In benchmarks, the instance demonstrates high parallel compute performance, excelling in multi-threaded tasks like Clang code compilation, Redis SET operations, and high-throughput static web serving. However, modest 2.5 GHz clock speeds and the lack of x86 vector extensions result in lower single-thread benchmark scores and constrained performance in large language model inference. The instance is well matched for scalable parallel tasks, including software build farms, caching clusters, and high-concurrency web tiers.
